source: Senatsverwaltung fuer Stadtentwicklung, Bauen und Wohnen
vv: VV Genehmigungskriterien soziale Erhaltungsgebiete, 7 April 2026, in force 18 April 2026

measures.label: Knock two flats into one
measures.rule: Merging flats is not approvable, and neither is splitting one. That holds even when the second half is newly built, such as a maisonette pushed up into the roof.
measures.why: A merged flat leaves the area with one home fewer, and the one that remains is bigger and dearer.

measures.label: Split one flat into two
measures.rule: Splitting a flat is not approvable. The rule is written as one sentence covering both splitting and merging, so there is no size at which it flips.
measures.why: Two small flats at a new rent replace one old tenancy, which is the fastest legal way to reset a price.

measures.label: Change the floor plan
measures.rule: A floor-plan change is only approvable when it is genuinely needed to bring the flat up to the standard of an average modern home, and then only to the minimum the building work requires. Changing the number of rooms, changing the floor area, adding box rooms, making an eat-in kitchen, or reworking a bathroom that is already complete all count as not needed.
measures.why: Most floor-plan work in a Berlin Altbau is not repair. It is a product change, and the borough treats it that way.

measures.label: Add a lift
measures.rule: In a building of four floors or fewer above ground, a new lift is not approvable. Above four floors it is approvable as normal modern equipment, unless it is unusually expensive or the area has an above-average displacement risk. A standard lift means bolted on outside, no stops between ground and first floor, a plain cabin at up to 1 m per second, a shaft no larger than 2.25 square metres, and a total cost under the published Berlin ceiling.
measures.why: A glass cabin in a four-storey block is not access. It is a rent rise with a door.

measures.label: Add a balcony or terrace
measures.rule: A first balcony, loggia, terrace or winter garden under 4 square metres is approvable when it is a standard build: a bolted-on galvanised steel frame, bar railings, a plain timber or composite deck, one door. A second one is not approvable if the flat already has any outdoor space, whatever its size or position. Replacing an existing balcony like for like is approvable.
measures.why: The cheap bolt-on balcony passes. The architectural one does not, because the rent rise it carries is the point.

measures.label: Put in a first bathroom
measures.rule: A first bathroom in standard build is approvable: one WC, one single hand basin, a bath or a shower, tiled walls and floor. A level-access shower, including a tray up to 3 cm deep, is approvable with a first fit-out or a full refit that amounts to one. Higher-standard parts are not approvable.
measures.why: This is the case the law was written to allow. A flat with no bathroom is below the modern standard, and fixing that is a right, not a favour.

measures.label: Add a second bathroom or WC
measures.rule: An extra bathroom, extra shower, extra bath or extra WC is not approvable. The single exception is a flat with at least five habitable rooms where the work does not change the room count.
measures.why: Two bathrooms is the standard marker of a flat aimed at a different income than the one already living there.

measures.label: Underfloor heating, a fireplace, high-end fittings
measures.rule: Creating especially high-value fit-out is not approvable. The list is explicit: underfloor heating, a fireplace, heating pipes hidden in the structure, stucco or panelling, high-grade parquet, stone or tiles, video entry phones, high-grade bathroom and kitchen fittings, a basin at least 80 cm wide or two basins, a level-access shower outside a first fit-out, a free-standing fixed kitchen island, floor-to-ceiling windows, and show entrances or stairwells. Wall-hung WCs, towel radiators and humidity-controlled extraction in an internal bathroom stay approvable.
measures.why: This is the clearest line in the whole rulebook, and it is the one landlords test most often.

measures.label: Insulation beyond the legal minimum
measures.rule: Energy work that goes past the minimum in the Gebaeudeenergiegesetz is not approvable unless it leaves tenants paying no more than the minimum version would, for example because a grant covers the difference. Insulating the top-floor ceiling and the cellar ceiling is approvable as low-cost work when it meets the federal BEG-EM U-value, whatever it costs and whether or not a grant is taken.
measures.why: The borough compares two modernisation surcharges side by side, the legal minimum against what is proposed, and the gap is what it refuses.

measures.label: Replace the heating system
measures.rule: From 1 July 2026 a swap is approvable in principle when the new system meets the 65 per cent renewable rule in section 71 of the Gebaeudeenergiegesetz and the old one is at least 15 years old, with no separate proof of breakdown needed. Under 15 years old, a swap is only approvable if the system is broken beyond repair or the early change costs tenants nothing extra. A connection to a heat network is approvable in principle.
measures.why: The date matters. The old wording asked for proof that the boiler was worn out; from July it asks how old it is.

measures.label: Solar panels on the roof or balcony
measures.rule: A roof array is approvable when all the power goes into the grid, or is sold to tenants as Mieterstrom, or when the owner leaves a third party to build and run it. If the owner runs it themselves and the power feeds lifts and stair lighting, it goes through the full check. A plug-in balcony panel needs no preservation permit at all.
measures.why: Your Balkonkraftwerk is outside this rulebook. That is worth knowing before anyone tells you otherwise.

measures.label: Demolish the building or a flat
measures.rule: Pulling down residential buildings or individual homes is not approvable. The rule is one sentence with no threshold and no exception written into it.
measures.why: The shortest clause in the document, and the reason a building that looks finished can still be standing.

measures.label: Turn the flat into an office, a shop or a holiday let
measures.rule: Changing a home to any other use is not approvable. Any change of purpose that stops the flat being available to people in the area for permanent living counts as a change of use.
measures.why: This is separate from the Zweckentfremdung rules and applies on its own inside the 82 areas.

measures.label: Let it furnished on a fixed term
measures.rule: Letting or subletting on a fixed term a home that was previously let open-ended counts as a change of use and needs an application, and the applicant carries the burden of proof. A fixed term under section 575 of the Civil Code is approvable in principle, and so is subletting your own registered main or second home for a period. Any other fixed term is not approvable, whether it is a head tenancy, a sublet or an intermediate let. The borough weighs the contract length, the furniture, what the tenant actually needs the flat for, whether the tenant asked for the fixed term or found it pre-printed, short break clauses, renewal options, the rent, whether anyone registers at the address, and extras such as a laundry service or a gym.
measures.why: This is the newest part of the rulebook, in force since 18 April 2026, and a Berlin court backed it on 10 September 2026.
